newsitem.title: GERMANY: German bank unions threaten action on sick pay.
newsitem.headline: German bank unions threaten action on sick pay.

text.p: Two German trade unions in the banking sector said on Wednesday they would stage industrial action from November 1 if banks went ahead with plans to cut sick payments to employees.

Deutsche Bank AG, Germany's largest commercial bank, said earlier this month it was implementing a new law envisaging a 20 percent cut in existing sick pay allowances. Commerzbank AG also said it would implement the law.

Gerhard Renner, chief of negotiations for the DAG white-collar union said after a meeting with the HBV banking union that employers had until November to back down on the cuts or face immediate protest action.
Workers would in the meantime be advised to do no further overtime, he added.

Bank employers believe that wage contracts in the sector allow them immediately to implement a new law cutting sick pay from 100 percent of salary to 80 percent without triggering the legal row seen in the engineering sector over the issue.
Around 460,000 people work in the German banking industry. Unions say that absenteeism in the sector is exceptionally low.
